The *Sivakattheraapadāna* (Tha Ap 561) is a verse text preserved in the *Therāpadāna* section of the Pali Khuddaka Nikāya [SuttaCentral]. It recounts the biographical narrative and past karmic deeds of the elder Sivaka. SuttaCentral registers five translations of the poem across five different languages [SuttaCentral]. No specific discussions of the text appear in the provided secondary literature dossier.

Textual parallels and reuse analyses from DharmaNexus indicate that the work shares extensive stock verses with other Pali texts, identifying 53 matching passages across 19 separate works [DharmaNexus]. Its most extensive overlap is preserved in the first volume of the commentary to the *Theragāthā* (*Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā*, Paṭhamo bhāgo), with 14 shared matches totaling 1,293 characters [DharmaNexus]. Within the *Therāpadāna* itself, repetitive poetic units are shared with several other apadāna texts, most notably the *Kummāsadāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 477), the *Nadīkassapattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 554), and the *Labujaphaladāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 469) [DharmaNexus]. Neither SuttaCentral nor DharmaNexus records any external cross-language parallels in Sanskrit, Chinese, or Tibetan corpora [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus].
